quoted_clause: Continuous batching (e.g. vLLM) is nearly mandatory to achieve the 1.2 s TTFT budget under 10 rps input-heavy traffic; without it, prefill of 9.2 K tokens per request would serialize and push TTFT well above 2 s.
observed: The sentence implies one 8×H100 host can serve the 10 rps average with continuous batching. But 10 rps × 9.2K input tokens = 92,000 prefill tokens/s, while the chapter's own sustained-planning prefill rate for one host is ~19,800 tok/s. Continuous batching cannot close a ~4.6× prefill-compute gap.
evidence: Ch 4 canonical box gives 10 rps and 9.2K input tokens; Ch 4 derivation notes and Ch 8 planning rate give ~19,800 tok/s per host. Ch 4 later says the canonical workload needs ~6 hosts at average and ~21 at peak.
root_cause: Conflates per-request feasibility with fleet capacity and overstates continuous batching as a substitute for prefill compute.
correction: State that one host is the per-request feasibility baseline, not the capacity answer. At 10 rps the fleet needs ~6 hosts; continuous batching improves utilization and latency but does not create prefill FLOPs.
acceptance_test: Recompute host count from 92,000 prefill tok/s and ~19,800 tok/s per host; the text must say ~6 hosts at average, not imply one host suffices.

page_hint: Ch 2 §6 (Architecture Consequence), decode levers and P/D paragraph
quoted_clause: higher-bandwidth memory topologies (NVSwitch, HBM3e) ... a decode cluster optimized for bandwidth (faster HBM, larger NVLink domains)
observed: NVSwitch and NVLink are inter-GPU interconnect technologies, not HBM memory bandwidth. HBM3e is per-GPU memory. The text conflates memory bandwidth with interconnect bandwidth.
evidence: The hardware hierarchy distinguishes per-GPU HBM bandwidth from NVLink/NVSwitch communication bandwidth. NVSwitch does not increase a GPU's HBM read rate; it helps sharded-model communication.
correction: Separate HBM3e (per-GPU memory bandwidth) from NVLink/NVSwitch (inter-GPU communication). Explain that NVSwitch helps tensor-parallel sharding, not single-GPU weight-read bandwidth.
acceptance_test: Replace the phrase with correct categories and add one sentence on when each helps; no clause may call NVSwitch a memory topology.

page_hint: Ch 4 §3, 'Arithmetic Walk-Through: From Users to Requests per Second'
quoted_clause: The step from '~2,000 registered users' to '~10 rps average' is the key connective tissue that makes the continuous scenario concrete. Here is the full derivation, traceable line by line: ... the ~10 rps average is declared as a scenario input ... not solved for from the 100-user population.
observed: The heading and introduction promise a derivation from users to rps, but step 3 says the 10 rps is declared and cannot be derived from the active-user population. The section is internally inconsistent about whether 10 rps is derived or assumed.
evidence: Little's Law cannot convert active-user population to arrival rate without a per-user request-frequency assumption. The text itself says this.
root_cause: Framing overpromises a derivation that the body correctly refuses to make.
correction: Rename the section 'From Users to Traffic Assumptions' or explicitly state that the per-user request frequency is the missing assumption. Show the arithmetic as an assumption, not a derivation from concurrency.
acceptance_test: The section no longer claims to derive 10 rps from 100 active users; it shows the per-user request-rate assumption and labels 10 rps as declared.

page_hint: Ch 3 §3, 'Why MoE saves compute but not KV cache memory'
quoted_clause: KV_per-token = 2 × n_layers × d_hidden × bytes-per-value ... for a GQA/MQA model substitute n_KV-heads × head_dim
observed: The formula uses d_hidden, but GQA/MQA require n_KV heads × d_head. Using d_hidden would overstate the KV width for GQA/MQA. The parenthetical correction is not reflected in the displayed formula.
evidence: Ch 1 gives the general formula with n_KV heads × d_head and defines d_hidden only for full MHA.
root_cause: Notation drift between the general and full-MHA forms.
correction: Write the general formula with n_KV heads × d_head and define d_hidden only for the full-MHA special case.
acceptance_test: The formula and the worked GQA example use the same symbol; substituting 8 KV heads × 128 gives the stated 0.0655 MB/token.

quoted_clause: The model is large enough to answer factual enterprise questions without fine-tuning
observed: No evidence or benchmark is given that a 70B dense model meets the >85% factual-accuracy target. The quality target is an assumption, not a demonstrated model property.
evidence: Table 4-1 labels the quality target [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]; no model evaluation is cited.
correction: Say that the canonical assumes a 70B dense model meets the quality target and that this must be validated against the quality dimension.
acceptance_test: The claim is tied to a quality evaluation or explicitly labeled as an assumption.

quoted_clause: Multi-region deployment (active-active) provides availability but doubles the infrastructure cost.
observed: Active-active multi-region can require more than 2× cost because of capacity duplication, replication, cross-region traffic, and failover policy. 'Doubles' is a lower-bound or illustrative estimate, not a general law.
evidence: The same bullet later says the topology is UNPRICED / NOT VALIDATED and must be costed separately.
root_cause: False precision in an operational-cost claim.
correction: Replace 'doubles' with 'can roughly double or more, depending on failover and replication policy; must be costed separately.'
acceptance_test: The sentence no longer asserts a universal 2× multiplier and cross-references the unpriced-topology caveat.

quoted_clause: Input-to-output ratio: 9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30× more input tokens than output tokens. This ratio is [canonical scenario][DERIVED] from the canonical numbers and is the single biggest factor in why this workload is KV-capacity- and prefill-dominated rather than decode-throughput-limited.
observed: The input/output ratio is a signal, not the single determinant. KV capacity depends on context length and concurrency; decode can dominate wall-clock latency even in input-heavy workloads. The chapter itself later says decode is ~87% of per-request wall-clock.
evidence: Ch 2 and Ch 4 both distinguish resource regime from wall-clock latency; measured per-phase utilization and goodput are required to confirm dominance.
correction: Soften to 'a first signal' and point to measured per-phase utilization and goodput before concluding dominance.
acceptance_test: The sentence no longer claims a single biggest factor; it cross-references Ch 2/Ch 8 and the need for measurement.

quoted_clause: a 70B FP16 model on one host meets the per-request latency SLO (TTFT/TPOT)
observed: Ch 2's arithmetic is a first-order analytical lower bound that excludes attention overhead, MFU, communication, and scheduling. 'Meets' overstates what has been shown.
evidence: Ch 2 repeatedly labels the arithmetic 'Analytical bound — not a benchmark'; Ch 4 later says both bounds must be confirmed by benchmark goodput.
root_cause: Claim strength exceeds the analytical evidence.
correction: Say 'is analytically feasible under the first-order model; benchmark confirmation is required.'
acceptance_test: The sentence carries the analytical/benchmark qualifier.

quoted_clause: From the token-level work alone (which we worked through in this chapter), the architect can already establish: ... the workload is input-heavy
observed: Token-level work defines the unit and the request shape, but it cannot establish that the workload is input-heavy. That requires the workload characterization in Ch 4 (prompt, retrieved context, output mix).
evidence: Ch 4 is where the token profile is quantified; Ch 1 only introduces the token as a unit.
correction: Say 'assuming the request shape includes retrieved context, the working hypothesis is input-heavy; Ch 4 quantifies it.'
acceptance_test: The mini-case distinguishes assumption from derivation and does not claim token-level work alone establishes input-heaviness.

page_hint: Ch 2 §1 'The work unit changes with the generator'; Ch 3 §1 'Alternative inference: the token is not the execution step'
quoted_clause: The prefill/decode split describes the autoregressive text path developed here. It does not describe every generative workload. ... Dense versus MoE describes parameter allocation. Autoregressive versus diffusion generation describes a different axis...
observed: The diffusion/video material is a multi-page digression that interrupts the core prefill/decode and dense-vs-MoE/KV threads before those mental models are consolidated. It introduces many new concepts (DDPM, SDE, flow matching, LLaDA, block diffusion, Wan2.2) at a point where the chapter promises a narrower architectural question.
evidence: Ch 2's Architect's Question is about prefill/decode and system constraints; Ch 3's is about dense vs MoE, total vs active parameters, and KV cache. The diffusion sections are not required for those core arguments.
correction: Move the diffusion/alternative-inference material to an appendix or a later chapter, or reduce it to a short scope note with a cross-reference.
acceptance_test: The main chapter threads flow from prefill/decode and dense/MoE to KV without a multi-page diffusion detour; the diffusion material has a clear home.

quoted_clause: At 10 concurrent full-context requests the MHA figure is ~241 GB of KV on top of the 140 GB weights — pressing against the 640 GB pool well before concurrency reaches 100.
observed: At 10 concurrent requests, 241 GB KV + 140 GB weights = 381 GB, leaving ~259 GB free. The pool is not 'pressing' at 10; it becomes tight around ~20 full-context requests.
correction: State the actual total at 10 requests and the approximate concurrency at which the pool tightens.
acceptance_test: The sentence gives 381 GB at 10 requests and says the pool tightens around ~20, not at 10.

quoted_clause: long enough for Little's Law and service-time occupancy to reach the modeled steady state (seconds of sustained 40 rps)
observed: Little's Law steady state requires at least the service-time scale W ≈ 8.6 s, not merely 'seconds.' A 2-second burst would not populate the queue to λ·W.
correction: Say 'for at least the service-time scale (~8.6 s), not a one-second spike.'
acceptance_test: The burst duration is tied to W_exec ≈ 8.6 s.

observed: The figure $155,816.93 carries cent-level precision for an illustrative included-cost input. The surrounding numbers are rounded estimates; the precision implies a derivation that is not shown.
evidence: The sidebar labels all four rows as illustrative included-cost inputs, not measured duty cycles.
